subject.title: [Bug] v2026.5.22 启动后 Gateway CPU 持续 100%+，导致请求延迟飙升 50-100 倍

question: Should normal gateway startup keep provider-auth prewarming default-on, or should it become hook-only/default-off with explicit opt-in for eager warming?
rationale: Current code can support both shapes, but the tradeoff affects upgrade behavior, auth-provider readiness, and startup responsiveness; automation should not choose that product contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt hook-only/default-off startup
options.body: Land or refresh the narrow PR so startup registers auth-failure rewarm hooks but does not run the initial provider-auth sweep unless explicitly enabled.

options.title: Keep default-on with documented opt-out
options.body: Treat the worker-thread mitigation plus OPENCLAW_SKIP_PROVIDER_AUTH_PREWARM as sufficient and document the operator tradeoff before closing related reports.

options.title: Reject the default change
options.body: Close the open candidate PR and keep eager startup warming as the intended contract, accepting the remaining startup CPU cost.

recommendation.title: Adopt hook-only/default-off startup
recommendation.body: Land or refresh the narrow PR so startup registers auth-failure rewarm hooks but does not run the initial provider-auth sweep unless explicitly enabled.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the open maintainer PR and the recent code path that added hook-only/env-controlled startup behavior.
